chunks: If a woman dies in postpartum bleeding and her blood is abundant, she is wrapped up to the navel in leather, or in something like clean leather; then after that she is shrouded, and the front private part and the anus are stuffed with cotton.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: When it is intended to place a woman into the grave, her bier is placed before it toward the qiblah, the coffin is lifted away from her, and she is taken from the bier sideways. Two people lower her into the grave: one places his hands beneath her shoulders, and the other his hands beneath her hips. It is preferable that the one who receives her from the side of her hips be her husband, or some of her blood relatives such as her father, her brother, or her son if she has no husband. A non-mahram should not undertake that except when her blood relatives are absent; and if women who know the procedure lower her into her grave, that is better.

1, 6 - (948) 116 - Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin, peace of Allah be upon him, said:
“The sunnah (prophetic tradition) established from رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم is that no one should enter a woman’s grave except one who used to see her during her lifetime.”

key_terms.الْأَدِيمِ: leather or leather-like material used here for wrapping
key_terms.تُكَفَّنُ: she is shrouded in burial cloth
key_terms.نُفَسَاءَ: a woman in postpartum bleeding after childbirth

ai.seo_question: Who may enter a woman's grave in Shia hadith, and how should a deceased woman be prepared for burial?
ai.summary: This report discusses rulings related to preparing and burying a deceased woman, especially one who dies in postpartum bleeding. It also transmits a sunnah from رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم that a woman’s grave should only be entered by someone who was permitted to see her during her lifetime, emphasizing burial etiquette and familial propriety.
